prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Enabling CTS sink clustering with a larger max diameter (200um instead of 100um) and larger cluster size (40 instead of 30) reduces clock tree buffer count and clock net routing demand, lowering global-route overflow while also shortening clock insertion delay variance so propagated-clock setup slack improves on all circuits — a CTS-stage (C1) probe independent of the partitioner.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.127 robust(mean-std)=-0.060 min_case=-0.055 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.054 dWNS=-3.3% dTNS=-6.9% overflow~151
  bp-ng45: score=-0.055 dWNS=-3.5% dTNS=-6.9% overflow~138
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.018 dWNS=-3.6% dTNS=-0.5% overflow~130
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis failed: all three cases show negative scores and worse WNS/TNS (dWNS −3.3% to −3.6%), with overflow still ~130–151, so larger sink clustering did not reduce buffer/routing demand or improve setup slack. The mechanism likely backfired—bigger clusters (40, 200µm) increase skew and insertion-delay spread rather than shorten it, hurting propagated-clock setup. Next step: sweep intermediate diameters (120–150µm) and cluster sizes (32–36) per case, and check clock skew/insertion-delay variance directly at C1 to confirm whether the clustering granularity is the true driver before retesting.
